title: Execution log v1 — the all-action audit trail
description: Validates the parsed form of V7/test_results/prompt_execution_log.md. Every controller action appends one record before it starts and one record when it ends: a completion ACT, or an EXEC whose Closes field names the start it terminates. The log is append-only and its ids are monotonic by construction. This schema exists because the previous run's logger was never proven correct before it recorded the entire run (failure B1) — the audit trail was the one thing that could not be audited.

records.description: In file order. Order is meaningful: the log is append-only and must never be reordered, rewritten or pruned.

unclosed_starts.description: Computed, not authored: every started ACT id, minus every id cited by a completion ACT or an EXEC Closes. Must be empty — zero unpaired starts is a release gate (LOG-PAIRED).

act.description: A successful action. Appended once when the action starts (status: started, result: pending) and once when it ends (status: completed or skipped, citing the started id).

action.description: A concrete controller or worker action — inspection, design, initialization, file creation, command, test, model call, render, source request, state transition, revision, audit, resume, terminal decision.

closes.description: On a completion or skipped record: the started ACT id this closes. Required unless status is 'started'. Never derived — always passed explicitly, because deriving it is exactly the B1 defect.

trigger.description: The exact command, state or gate that caused this action.

result.description: 'pending' on a started record; a concrete measured result on a completion.

notes.description: Optional. Elapsed time, hashes, model and effort, command exit code, linked EXEC id. Never load-bearing — anything a gate depends on is a required field, not a note.

exec.description: A failed action. Terminates exactly one started ACT, named in closes — mandatory, because the pairing gate cannot be computed from free text.

closes.description: The started ACT id this failure terminates. Required, never blank. An EXEC whose closes does not resolve is itself a logging failure and stops the run as META_SYSTEM_FAILURE.

then.description: 'other' must state the reason in notes, or the taxonomy is a wildcard.
